subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a plugin-facing synchronous config-write veto, and what ordering, trust, failure, and metadata contract should it have before persisted config writes?
rationale: This would let plugin code block security-sensitive persisted configuration changes, so automation cannot safely choose the public API boundary or fail-closed behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a guarded config-write veto
options.body: Approve a narrow hook/API contract with current and pending config, changed paths, actor metadata, base hash, typed reject result, timeout/recursion rules, and tests for all config write paths.

options.title: Keep validation in core/doctor only
options.body: Reject plugin veto power for now and continue adding built-in validators, doctor checks, and agent-tool allowlists for known dangerous config changes.

options.title: Route through a broader preflight RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of a wider config validation/mutation framework that also covers boot-time preflight and rollback behavior.

recommendation.title: Design a guarded config-write veto
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow hook/API contract with current and pending config, changed paths, actor metadata, base hash, typed reject result, timeout/recursion rules, and tests for all config write paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the clearest existing product/security review for this issue and have recent config-write/security history.
